"en": "Historical medicinal-plant manual: section 9 distinguishes water from loss on drying; not the 2011 edition, a universal extract limit or market authorization.",

"text": "A supplier’s “moisture” line is incomplete without the test method. Loss on drying (LOD) measures mass lost under specified drying conditions, not water alone: WHO’s 1998 medicinal-plant manual explicitly includes both water and volatile matter.[1] For procurement, ask whether the agreed attribute is drying loss or water content before comparing two COAs. This historical manual explains a measurement distinction; it does not establish a current specification for every finished extract."

"text": "Q3C allows a nonspecific method such as loss on drying when only Class 3 solvents are present and the method is properly validated.[1] That qualified statement is not a license to identify individual solvents from an unexplained LOD value. Equally, it would be wrong to claim Q3C always requires headspace GC for every extract. Request the laboratory’s documented rationale for the chosen procedure and the actual acceptance question."

"text": "Request the exact correction formula and the measurement used in it. If the laboratory uses loss on drying, ask what procedure generated that value and whether it was measured on a representative sample from the same lot. If a water-specific result is used instead, record that distinction. These are different reporting choices; this guide does not supply a universal correction factor or prescribe a moisture method for every extract."
